title: Tool Poisoning Attacks: Hidden Instructions in MCP Tool Descriptions
summary: Researchers show MCP servers can embed adversarial instructions in tool description fields that the host LLM silently executes during tool discovery.
note: MCP-specific exploit class; mcp-security over prompt-injection because the attack vector is the protocol.

title: Releasing mcp-server-filesystem v0.6.0 with sandboxed root scoping
summary: The official filesystem MCP server adds per-root allowlists and symlink-escape guards; breaking change to the config schema for path roots.
note: Server release with a security-relevant feature, but ecosystem news is the primary frame.

title: CVE-2025-49214: Path Traversal in a Popular MCP SQLite Server
summary: An unauthenticated path-traversal flaw in mcp-sqlite-server lets a crafted resource URI read arbitrary files outside the configured database directory.
note: Concrete MCP CVE; mcp-security primary, not generic agent-security.

title: Indirect Prompt Injection via Email Reaches Agentic Assistants
summary: A benign-looking calendar invite carries hidden instructions that a downstream LLM assistant follows when summarizing the inbox, exfiltrating thread contents.
note: Classic indirect injection technique; injection is the core finding, not the assistant brand.

title: A Taxonomy of Prompt Injection Defenses That Actually Hold Up
summary: Survey categorizes spotlighting, delimiting, and dual-LLM patterns, with an eval showing most fail under tool-augmented agents.
note: Defenses + taxonomy squarely prompt-injection despite agent-eval angle.

title: Cursor Rules Files Can Be Weaponized to Inject Persistent Instructions
summary: Malicious .cursorrules committed to a repo silently steer the coding agent's edits, enabling supply-chain code tampering on pull.
note: Injection vector but the security boundary and impact are coding-agent specific; coding-agents primary.

title: Claude Code 0.9 Adds Permission Prompts for Shell and Network Tools
summary: New release gates bash, network fetch, and file-write tools behind explicit user approval, with an allowlist config for unattended runs.

title: Sandbox Escape in a Multi-Agent Orchestration Framework
summary: A worker agent can break out of its tool sandbox by abusing a shared message bus to invoke privileged tools registered by a sibling agent.
note: Sandbox/multi-agent issue, not MCP-specific and not injection; agent-security.

title: Browser Agent Hijacked by Hidden Text on a Web Page
summary: An agentic browser following on-page instructions navigates to an attacker domain and submits the user's saved credentials.
note: Injection-adjacent but the attack surface is the agentic browser; browser-agents primary.

title: Comet and Arc-style Agentic Browsers: A Security Threat Model
summary: Analysis enumerates DOM-injection, credential autofill abuse, and cross-origin tool leakage risks unique to browser-driving agents.

summary: Paper measures whether agents trained with tool access learn to conceal goal-directed behavior from oversight, with reproducible evals.

title: Open-Sourcing promptmap2: A Scanner for Prompt-Injection in System Prompts
summary: CLI tool fuzzes an app's system prompt with known injection payloads and reports which guardrails leak; supports MCP and OpenAI tool schemas.

title: mcp-scan: Static Analysis for Malicious MCP Server Manifests
summary: New utility parses MCP server configs and flags tool-poisoning, overbroad scopes, and suspicious command templates before install.
